These events and the nuclear test that followed motivated a global effort to constrain nuclear arms. In this regard, the Comprehensive Nuclear Test Ban Treaty is one of the key pillars of the international disarmament and non-proliferation architecture, contributing to global peace and security. The treaty's strong legitimacy and vital importance for our collective security is pointed out in UN Security Council Resolution 2310, and the annual General Assembly resolutions relating to the CTBT. Since its opening for signature in 1996, the CTBT has served to limit nuclear testing in an unprecedented way, complementing the NPT and serving as a strong confidence and security building measure. Nuclear test explosions represent a serious danger to international peace and security. The cessation of all nuclear weapon test explosions and all other nuclear explosions by constraining the development and qualitative improvement of nuclear weapons and ending the development of advanced new types of nuclear weapons constitute an effective measure of nuclear disarmament and non-proliferation in all its aspects. The CTBT entry into force remains a top priority for the European Union. It would codify the global norm against nuclear weapon test explosions or any other nuclear explosion and reinforce international peace and security. This high-level meeting provides another opportunity to call for the treaty's prompt entry into force and universalization. All EU member states have ratified the treaty and consistently called upon all states that have not done so, in particular the remaining Annex II states, to sign and ratify the CTBT without any preconditions or further delay. We continue to deeply deplore the unprecedented decision by the Russian Federation, contrary to its NPT and other commitments, to revoke its ratification of the CTBT. This moves us collectively further away from the entry into force of the treaty. In the meantime, it is crucial for international peace and security that all states fully observe the moratorium on nuclear test explosions or any other nuclear explosions and refrain from any action contrary to the object and purpose of the treaty. In this regard, we call on all states to continue to honor their engagements and reaffirm their commitments. Mr. President, The current security environment is increasingly fragile, marked by Russia's full-scale invasion of Ukraine and its systematic undermining of the arms control architecture. The EU condemns in the strongest possible terms Russia's actions, irresponsible nuclear rhetoric, and threats to use nuclear force in its illegal, unjustified, and unprovoked war of aggression against Ukraine, which are provocative, dangerous, and escalatory. Russia's so-called suspensions of its implementation of the New START Treaty and its statement on the denuclearization of the DPRK as a closed issue, in clear violation of relevant UN Security Council resolutions, further erode trust in international non-proliferation and disarmament regime. In this context, Russia must immediately and unconditionally withdraw all its forces and military equipment from the entire territory of Ukraine and fully respect Ukraine's territorial integrity sovereignty and independence within its internationally recognized borders. No state should conduct nuclear weapons test explosions or any other nuclear explosions. The EU urges the DPRK to comply with its obligations and the relevant UN Security Council resolutions, to refrain from testing nuclear devices and ballistic missiles, reaffirm the moratorium on long-range ballistic missiles and nuclear tests, and sign and ratify the CBTB without any preconditions or further delay. We urge the DPRK to abandon its existing nuclear weapons program, as well as programs to build delivery systems and other weapons of mass destruction in a complete, verifiable, and irreversible manner, as required by UN Security Council resolutions. Any nuclear test must be met with a swift, united, and robust international response. The EU stands ready to support any meaningful diplomatic process and is committed to working with all relevant partners to build a basis for sustainable peace and security and take steps aimed at pursuing complete, verifiable, irreversible denuclearization of the Korean peninsula. Following the DPRK's previous six nuclear tests, the CTBTO demonstrated its invaluable role in quickly providing reliable and independent data enabling the international community to respond appropriately and swiftly. The CTBTO has provided the world with a truly global high-tech monitoring system for nuclear explosions, something that no single state could do. The EU reiterates its confidence in the CTBT's verification regimes and looks forward to the completion of the international monitoring system. We recognize its deterrence effect against non-compliance with the treaty and its ability to respond to threats to international peace and security. Ensuring the sustainability and effectiveness of the verification regime through adequate funding remains crucial. Mr. President, in addition to the CTBT's obvious contribution to international peace and security, the EU advocates fully exploiting the potential benefits of civil and scientific applications of IMS data. In this regard, the EU financially supports the CTBTO's verification regime and integrated capacity building activities in developing countries. Since 2006, the EU has provided the CBTTO with voluntary contributions of more than 29.5 million euros and will continue to do so. Finally, the EU continues to support and actively promote the entry into force of the CBT in line with action 25 of the pact for the future. And in this regard, we praise the efforts of the Article 14 coordinators, Norway and Panama, and welcome the continuous efforts of the group of friends of the CTTB towards entry into force and universality. The EU reaffirms its commitment to the CTTB and will continue to seize every opportunity to call for CTTB's prompt entry into force in all relevant international fora and in meetings with the countries that have not yet signed or ratified the treaty, notably the remaining Annex II States. We look forward to the next Article 14 Conference, led by incoming Presidency Sweden and the Philippines, as an important opportunity to promote such treaty. Thank you.

Thank you very much. We have heard the last speaker for this meeting. The right of reply has been requested. I would like to remind you that statements in the exercise of the right of reply are limited to ten minutes for the first intervention and five minutes for the second, and delegations should make those statements from their seats. I give the floor to Israel.

Thank you, Mr. President. Despite our initial hope that today's meeting would remain professional and focused on the pressing challenges before us, we are regrettably compelled to respond to the unfounded and absurd statements made earlier today. The Middle East continues to face a chronic lack of compliance with non-proliferation and arms control norms, obligations, and mechanisms. Certain states in the region deliberately violates their commitments to international treaties and frameworks. Ironically, those at the very top of the global noncompliance index are often the loudest in casting accusations outward. Iran is in no moral position to lecture or preach about nuclear threats. For decades, the Iranian regime has relied on lies and deception to conceal its true intentions, systematically violating its commitments under the NPT and other international disarmament frameworks, all while fueling regional and global instability, chaos, and terror. Operation Rising Lion. took place in the context of an ongoing armed conflict between Israel and Iran and aimed to neutralize the existential and imminent threat to Israel's very existence, the Iranian regime nuclear weapons and ballistic missile program. The regime has accelerated its nuclear weapons program while simultaneously investing in long-range ballistic missiles. Israel acted to prevent further direct attacks by the regime, including the launching of ballistic missiles and hundreds of UAVs towards densely populated areas in Israel, deliberately targeting civilians and civilian infrastructures, and tragically resulting in civilian casualties. In contrast to the Iranian terrorist regime, Israel's military operations were in full accordance with the law of armed conflict, taking into account extensive precautionary measures. While the operation has been completed, Israel's fight to defend its citizens and territory continues. Israel remains under attack from the Iranian regime proxies and affiliated non-state armed groups, and will continue to defend its territory and people from the threat posed by the regime and terrorist groups in the region.
I thank you, Mr. President. I give the floor to the Islamic Republic of Iran.

Thank you, Mr. President. In response to the absurd allegations made by Israeli representative -- Israeli regime representative, I would like to highlight the following: Iran's nuclear program has always been exclusively peaceful in nature and has remained subject to the most rigorous oversight of the International Atomic Energy Agency. For over three decades, the Zionist regime has propagated the claim that Iran seeks to develop nuclear weapons, thereby deceiving certain states and manipulating public opinion. But where, indeed, is this alleged nuclear bomb? This reflects the infamous Nazi propaganda method. A lie told once remains lie, but a lie repeated a thousand times begins to be accepted as truth. The international community must not allow such fabrications to distort reality. Is it not patently absurd that a regime which itself possesses every category of weapons of mass destruction, is party to none of the relevant international instruments, and whose eight decades record is replete with aggression, atrocity, and genocide, now levels unfounded accusations against a state party to the NPT? Mr. President, the Israeli regime, which has gone so far as to weaponize even food and water against innocent civilians in Gaza, has over the past eight decades carried out more than 3,000 terrorist operations, displaced over seven million Palestinians, martyred and wounded hundreds of thousands, and imprisoned more than one million Palestinians. This is the very same regime that has launched military aggressions against its neighbors, remains a party to none of the international instruments on disarmament and non-proliferation of weapons of mass destruction, and maintains hundreds of nuclear warheads in its arsenal. And you are all aware of the catastrophic consequences that the possession of nuclear weapons by such a criminal regime entails for international peace and security. Mr. President, distinguished delegates, the Israeli regime, which has gone so far as to weaponize even food and water against innocent civilians in Gaza, and burdened by such a dark record, lacks any credibility to lecture others on international law or the observance of obligations.

I thank you, Mr. President.
May I take it that the Assembly wishes to conclude its consideration of agenda item 98? It is so decided. The meeting stands adjourned.
